mechanisms.statement: Think-SFT imitates teacher traces written without a token budget that almost never end in an underived number, so it keeps deriving until it reaches an answer. At 16,384 tokens its errors are mostly unfinished work, not guesses, and its finished answers are far more often right than RL's. More tokens convert its cut answers at about a quarter, and its vote is nearly pass@k because cut samples abstain instead of voting wrong.

holds_against.why: RL finishing Think-SFT's cut prefixes gets no more right than Think-SFT: at the cut the derivation is incomplete, so forcing an end gives guesses; with 16k more tokens 23 of 93 become right.
On MATH-500 cap-hit problems of the base, RL also finishes and solves them, so persistence has nothing extra to win there; it pays only on long hard problems.

forecasts.reason: Code problems are short, so the cap rarely binds and persistence costs little; Think-SFT lands near RL-Code's 401 minus a few cut traces.

mechanisms.statement: Outcome reward pays only for a correct, parsable answer completed inside the rollout budget, so the RL gradient concentrates in a few weight directions that make the model commit to its current best derivation, check it and box it. Their size sets how often it finishes and also raises right answers on problems it already finishes, bounded by what the host can derive. A host tolerates them up to a size set by its own training; past that, text degrades.

holds_against.why: IF's 8 directions close answers (41 cap hits) but add no right math answers: IF's reward verified format, not math, so its commitment has no math derivation behind it.
Top-1 at 3x finishes (10 cap hits) yet loses right answers and stops boxing: past the base's tolerance the push degrades text, as stated.

mechanisms.statement: Pretraining on reasoning-style text left the base a deliberative register ('Okay', first-person checking) that it already enters in some draws; the cue, a self-chosen opening, and the first steps of any verifiable-reward RL select it rather than add skill. On a plain prompt an edit's score therefore rises with how strongly it writes the opening, a steep logistic in edit size, up to the cued base's level; gains beyond that come from other parts of training.

holds_against.why: Code-RL on the math plain prompt reaches 390, 60 below its cued 450: a code-only reward installs the opening on most but not all math answers, so code directions sit below Math top-8's 427 on the plain prompt.

mechanisms.statement: Imitation of other models' text (Think-SFT, 25 % of weight norm) and outcome-reward RL on the model's own samples (0.24 %) optimise unrelated objectives, so their weight changes are orthogonal and compose: the RL difference does on Think-SFT what it does on the base, closing answers, while Think-SFT keeps its precision. Math and Code reward directions, and layer bands, add their gains along a shared closing subspace until closing saturates; beyond that extra dose only lowers precision.
